annotations.text:
THE PROBLEM IN ONE LINE

The Overview reports the day but never judges it. Eight equal-weight panels, every number absolute, nothing ranked — so "is today staffed?" takes a full scroll and some arithmetic.

The fix isn't more charts. It's a hierarchy: verdict → exceptions → context.

PROPOSED — same design system, same data, re-ranked

1. A status bar that states the verdict before any number.
2. KPI tiles that carry a sparkline + delta, so 89% can be read as good or bad.
3. An action queue that finally NAMES the missions with no crew (today they're a number in a subtitle).
4. Contract-mix donuts folded into the By-board table as one column — 7 donuts become 1 column at 6 boards.
5. The two near-identical trend charts merged into one with a metric switcher; the 600-character caption moves behind an ⓘ.

IF YOU BUILD ONLY ONE THING

List the unstaffed missions. It's the highest-value change on the page and the cheapest — the count is already computed in boardStats(), the mission rows are already in memory, and it's the only item here that changes what someone does in the next ten minutes.

Second: the sparkline + delta on the utilization tile. The 14 days are already fetched for the chart below it.

None of the five modules needs a schema change. Four are pure client-side arithmetic on data already in memory; the fifth (host coverage risk) reads the deployment_history table added this week — the same rows as the Host Record tab, aggregated by host instead of by employee.

Sample figures throughout are realistic placeholders, not live data: 128 staff, 21 missions, 2 boards.
